title: Persistent Mini-Globals as Struct Fields
pattern: A struct contains private member variables that are only used as temporary "scratchpads" to pass data between private methods of a single call chain, rather than being passed as local parameters.
why_bad: The fields become "mini-globals" inside the class boundary. This unnecessarily increases the persistent footprint of the struct, prevents the struct from being thread-safe, and obscures which fields represent actual long-term object state vs. short-lived calculations.
detection: Identify struct fields that are written to in one method and subsequently read in other methods, but have no meaningful lifetime beyond a single, cohesive high-level method invocation.
fix:
Demote the temporary fields to local variables inside the caller method and pass them explicitly to private helper methods as arguments.
```rust
// Field removed from struct definition, passed as explicit local parameter instead.
```
source: *The Art of Readable Code* by Dustin Boswell and Trevor Foucher (Chapter 9, "Shrink the Scope of Your Variables", "Mini-Globals").
